suffix_ownership: 4.3.25 selects a locative base in the birth relation. The Nyāsa connects the star-named time with 4.2.3–4, and the individual stars have their own source number, e.g. śraviṣṭhāsu but phalgunyoḥ. This number does not constrain the number of the resulting person.
4.3.34 gives luk of the natal taddhita in the ten listed cases. 1.2.49 removes an existing subordinate feminine when the taddhita has luk; only inputs actually carrying such an affix can lose it.

For a woman born under Citrā, Revatī or Rohiṇī the recorded vārttika extends luk. The original feminine is removed and a new affix is licensed for the sex of the person. Ṭāp for Citrā; ṅīṣ for Revatī and Rohiṇī. The Kāśikā says gaurādi. The Kaumudī invokes the open pippalyādi and the Tattvabodhinī notes the open gaurādi account.

For phalgunī a specifically prescribed ṭa authorizes ṅīp through its marker; for aṣāḍhā an and subsequent ṭāp. Nyāsa attributes the initial-accent purpose to n of an. On the masculine schedules for Śraviṣṭhā and Aṣāḍhā an additional chaṇ gives lengthened initial and īya. These are alternative words in the same case–number request.

source_limits.bhāṣya: Three proposals are discussed at 4.3.34. The concluding na vā answers that the broad prescription of luk can account for the issue; retain the objection alongside the Kāśikā’s explicit examples.
source_limits.svāti: Kāśikā’s actual masculine example is svātiḥ. Tattvabodhinī records Kaiyaṭa/Haradatta with a short-i input; Mādhava reads long ī. On the latter interpretation a separate non-ṅīṣ input can have sauvāta. No unrestricted doublet is inferred for every svāti request.
source_limits.other_natal_dictionaries: Apte also lists rauhiṇa/rauhiṇī in the birth sense. The distinct affix and lexical head are observed here, without putting that separate head into every Rohiṇī natal cell.

source_models: Five head-specific inflection tables supply 120 cells. The other heads reuse the appropriate a, ā, i, ī, or u schedule. Tiṣya takes retroflex ending ṇ in tiṣyeṇa, while a dental is required after the intervening consonants in hastena, śraviṣṭhena and punarvasunā.
